overview: A WS2812B ('NeoPixel' is Adafruit's brand name for the same chip) is an RGB LED with its own tiny controller chip built directly into the package, letting hundreds of them be chained on a single data wire — each pixel reads the color data meant for it, then passes the rest down the line to the next pixel. That single-wire chaining is the entire point: no separate wire per LED, no shift registers, just one data pin controlling an entire strip or matrix of individually addressable, full-color pixels. The precise timing this protocol requires means it's typically driven by a dedicated library (FastLED, Adafruit NeoPixel) rather than simple digitalWrite calls.
simpleSummary: Individually-controllable color LEDs that can be chained together and run off a single data wire.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 5V (logic and LED power combined on most strips)
specifications.colorDepth: 24-bit RGB (8 bits per channel) per pixel
specifications.currentPerPixel: Up to ~60 mA at full white brightness — adds up fast across many pixels
specifications.chaining: Data-in on one pixel connects to data-out of the previous, forming a chain of any length

pinMap.name: 5V
pinMap.function: Power input, shared across the whole strip/chain.
pinMap.currentLimit: Up to ~60mA per pixel at full white — a 60-pixel strip at full brightness can need 3.6A+
pinMap.gotcha: Long strips at high brightness need a dedicated power supply, not a microcontroller's onboard 5V pin — undersized power causes dim or flickering far-end pixels and color inaccuracy from voltage drop.

pinMap.name: GND
pinMap.function: Ground reference, shared with the controlling microcontroller.

pinMap.name: DIN
pinMap.function: Data input — receives the precisely-timed single-wire protocol carrying color data for this pixel and everything after it.
pinMap.gotcha: On a 3.3V microcontroller (ESP32, etc.), the data signal often needs a level shifter to reliably read as HIGH by the 5V-logic LEDs, especially on longer strips.

pinMap.name: DOUT
pinMap.function: Data output — passes the remaining color data down the chain to the next pixel.

useCases.title: Addressable LED strip lighting
useCases.scenario: Animated, individually-colored lighting effects for a room, costume, or vehicle.

useCases.title: Robot status indicator
useCases.scenario: Use color/pattern changes to communicate a robot's internal state (idle, moving, error) at a glance.

useCases.title: LED matrix display
useCases.scenario: Arrange many pixels in a grid for simple graphics, scrolling text, or a VU meter.

oftenConfusedWith: Standard RGB LEDs (need 3 separate control pins per LED, no chaining/addressing)
oftenUpgradedTo: SK9822/APA102 (adds a separate clock line for more consistent timing on very long strips)
